answer: Each epoch the network publishes a fresh seed and every agent must solve a memory-hard puzzle keyed to its identity and that seed: an Argon2-style computation holding 4 GB of RAM sixty seconds, yielding a proof peers verify in milliseconds. A haven of honest agents spends one minute of memory it already owns, while a farm running 1,000 fakes must hold 4 TB of RAM, about $40,000 in hardware or $8,000 a month rented. Three random peers check each proof against the seed and the copper seal of the agent's key; a reused proof is rejected, the identity frozen three epochs, its sable entry void.
